name: ADLs / Personal Care
anchors: Independent in basic ADLs; no routine staff help
Cueing/setup or occasional minimal help in 1 ADL
Regular hands-on help in 1–2 ADLs
Extensive hands-on help across multiple ADLs
Near-total/total dependence across most basic ADLs
evidenceRequired: Specify which ADLs + assistance type + frequency
calibrationNote: Score resident need regardless of whether LifeCare staff or PCG performs it
scope: Bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, eating, continence, transfers
goalDefaults: Maintain independence with personal care and respect the resident's preferred routines, timing and choices.
Maintain independence with self-care, providing occasional setup or cueing as needed while respecting preferred routines and choices.
Maximize participation in personal care while providing regular hands-on assistance as needed. Maintain privacy, dignity and preferred routines.
Encourage the resident to participate in personal care to the extent safely possible while providing extensive assistance across needed ADLs. Preserve dignity and personal choices.
Maintain comfort, dignity and personal preferences during all personal care. Encourage any safe participation despite extensive dependence.
interventionDefaults: Allow resident to complete bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting and eating independently.
Set out preferred toiletries/clothing only if requested.
Respect usual timing, sequence, privacy and cultural preferences.
Observe for new difficulty, fatigue, pain or decline during self-care.
Provide setup for selected ADLs (e.g., clothing, toiletries, meal tray).
Give one-step reminders or verbal cueing only when needed.
Encourage resident to complete remaining steps independently.
Document which ADLs needed cueing/setup and any change from baseline.
Provide hands-on help for identified ADLs while allowing resident to perform safe steps.
Use agreed transfer/body mechanics during bathing, dressing and toileting.
Offer simple choices for clothing, grooming and timing.
Check skin and comfort during personal care and report concerns.
Provide extensive hands-on assistance across multiple ADLs using a consistent sequence.
Prepare all supplies before care and cluster tasks to reduce fatigue.
Encourage participation in any safe step (face washing, arm through sleeve, self-feeding portions).
Complete post-care comfort, hygiene and skin checks.
Provide near-total/total assistance for personal care while protecting privacy and dignity.
Use two-person/mechanical assistance when required by the care plan and trained staff.
Reposition and provide comfort measures during/after care.
Offer meaningful choices and observe non-verbal signs of pain or distress.

name: Mobility / Transfers
anchors: Independent safe transfers/ambulation
Device/setup or intermittent standby
Recurring supervision/contact guard/minimal physical assist
Substantial physical assist or complex transfers; frequent mobility help
Near-total mobility dependence / non-ambulatory with extensive transfer support
evidenceRequired: Transfer method, assist level, device, frequency
calibrationNote: Wheelchair availability alone does not equal 4
scope: Ambulation, transfer assistance, gait, balance, assistive devices
goalDefaults: Maintain safe, independent mobility and transfers at the resident's preferred pace and routine.
Maintain safe mobility with appropriate device, setup or intermittent standby assistance while preserving independence.
Promote safe mobility and transfers with supervision, contact guard or minimal assistance as needed. Encourage active participation and independence.
Maintain safe mobility and transfers using the established assistance level, technique and equipment while encouraging participation as tolerated.
Ensure safe and comfortable transfers and mobility with extensive assistance while preserving dignity, comfort and any remaining functional ability.
interventionDefaults: Encourage independent walking and transfers at usual pace.
Keep usual mobility route uncluttered and footwear accessible.
Ensure commonly used items are within safe reach.
Observe for new gait, endurance or transfer changes.
Set up prescribed mobility device before ambulation.
Provide standby assistance for transfers or longer walks as identified.
Remind resident to use device/handrails and appropriate footwear.
Document episodes requiring more than standby help.
Provide recurring supervision/contact guard or minimal assist for transfers and ambulation.
Use the same transfer technique and cue sequence across staff.
Position mobility device correctly before standing/sitting.
Monitor gait, balance, fatigue and dizziness during mobility.
Provide substantial physical assistance for transfers and frequent mobility help.
Use gait belt/device only if approved by policy/care plan and staff are trained.
Plan toileting/meals to reduce unnecessary high-risk transfers.
Coordinate mobility technique with nurse/PT/OT and document tolerance.
Provide extensive transfer/mobility support according to the established safe-handling plan.
Use mechanical/two-person transfer when required and available within capability.
Reposition regularly and support comfort in bed/chair.
Check for pain, skin pressure and tolerance after transfers.

name: Fall Risk
anchors: No material identified fall risk
Low risk; routine prevention only
Moderate risk requiring individualized precautions
High risk requiring regular supervision/assistance during risk activities
Very high/recurrent unsafe mobility despite controls; intensive prevention
calibrationNote: Fall risk alone is a modifier; do not use score as automatic LOC floor
scope: History, gait/balance, medications/risk factors, environmental contributors
goalDefaults: Maintain safe independent mobility using routine fall-prevention measures and a safe environment.
Maintain safe mobility and prevent falls through routine precautions while preserving independence.
Reduce fall risk through individualized precautions, appropriate assistance and monitoring of gait, balance and contributing factors.
Prevent falls and injury through regular supervision or assistance during identified risk activities while supporting safe mobility.
Minimize falls and injury through intensive individualized prevention, close supervision and the least restrictive safety measures appropriate to the resident.
interventionDefaults: Maintain clear pathways, adequate lighting and safe footwear.
Keep call system/personal items within reach.
Encourage usual safe mobility habits.
Record any new fall or near-fall.
Complete routine fall-prevention check each shift/day per policy.
Remind resident to use mobility device and avoid rushing.
Ensure room/bathroom setup supports safe movement.
Review any near-fall for contributing factors.
Implement individualized fall precautions documented in the care plan.
Provide assistance for identified high-risk activities (toileting, transfers, showering).
Monitor gait, balance, footwear, device use and environmental contributors.
Review medications/clinical contributors with nurse when risk changes.
Provide regular supervision/assistance during mobility and identified risk periods.
Schedule proactive toileting and respond promptly to mobility needs.
Use individualized cues/redirection to prevent unsafe unassisted movement.
Complete post-fall/near-fall review and update interventions.
Maintain intensive individualized fall-prevention plan using least restrictive measures.
Provide close supervision during all high-risk mobility/transfers.
Use team handoff of current triggers, safest techniques and recent events.
Escalate promptly after falls, head impact, acute change or inability to maintain safety.

name: Cognition
anchors: Intact cognition/self-direction for daily care
Mild forgetfulness; occasional cueing
Regular cueing/reorientation; some impaired judgment
Substantial impairment affecting multiple daily-care decisions
Severe impairment with inability to self-direct care and pervasive support need
evidenceRequired: Examples of cueing, judgment, orientation and self-direction
calibrationNote: Diagnosis of dementia alone does not determine score
scope: Orientation, memory, judgment, ability to follow directions
goalDefaults: Maintain autonomy, self-direction and participation in daily decisions and preferred routines.
Support independence and orientation with occasional reminders or cueing while allowing adequate time for decision-making.
Maintain participation in daily routines through regular cueing, reorientation and support with decisions while respecting the resident's choices.
Promote comfort and participation through structured routines, simple choices, familiar approaches and substantial support with daily-care decisions.
Maintain comfort, dignity and familiarity through consistent routines, simple communication and pervasive support with daily care and decision-making.
interventionDefaults: Offer normal choices and involve resident directly in decisions.
Maintain preferred routine and access to calendar/clock as desired.
Communicate changes in schedule clearly.
Observe for acute confusion or new memory difficulty.
Give occasional reminders for appointments, meals or daily routine.
Use one-step cueing when resident loses track of a task.
Allow extra processing time before repeating instructions.
Document new or increasing cueing needs.
Provide regular cueing/reorientation using familiar language and routines.
Offer limited, simple choices to preserve decision-making.
Supervise decisions involving safety, medication and high-risk activities as care plan indicates.
Use consistent staff approaches and document effective cues.
Use structured daily routine and repeated simple cues for most care activities.
Break tasks into one-step directions and demonstrate when helpful.
Anticipate needs when resident cannot reliably plan/sequence care.
Record behavior/cognition patterns that affect care delivery.
Provide pervasive support for daily decisions and care sequencing.
Use simple language, non-verbal cues and consistent familiar routines.
Anticipate basic needs while still offering simple choices and seeking assent.
Monitor non-verbal indicators of pain, fear, hunger or toileting need.

name: Behavior / BPSD
anchors: No care-impacting behavior
Rare/mild behavior managed with routine approach
Recurring behavior requiring planned redirection
Frequent behavior materially affecting care/safety
Persistent/severe behavior requiring intensive individualized management
calibrationNote: Score current care burden, not historical diagnosis alone

goalDefaults: Maintain emotional well-being, meaningful relationships, preferred activities and usual routines.

Reduce distress and maintain safety through frequent individualized reassurance, redirection and de-escalation while preserving dignity and choice.
Maintain safety, comfort and dignity through intensive person-centered behavioral support using individualized triggers, calming strategies and the least restrictive approach.
interventionDefaults: Support preferred social activities, hobbies and family contact.
Respect privacy, coping style and desired level of engagement.
Offer normal choices without forcing participation.
Observe for new anxiety, withdrawal, agitation or mood change.
Provide occasional reassurance/redirection during distress.
Use known calming activities and preferred communication style.
Identify and document triggers when episodes occur.
Return resident to preferred activity/routine after distress resolves.
Maintain predictable routine and proactively reduce known triggers.
Use individualized reassurance, redirection and de-escalation plan.
Offer meaningful activity matched to ability and preference.
Document antecedent, behavior, response and effective intervention.
Provide frequent individualized de-escalation/redirection and close follow-through.
Assign consistent approaches and communicate triggers/effective responses at handoff.
Modify environment/activity promptly when distress escalates.
Coordinate clinical review for new or worsening behavior.
Implement intensive person-centered behavior support plan using least restrictive approaches.
Maintain high consistency of routine, staffing approach and environment.
Use proactive comfort checks and individualized calming/sensory strategies.
Escalate urgently when behavior suggests pain, delirium, medication effect or imminent harm.

name: Clinical Monitoring
anchors: Stable; routine wellness observation only
One stable condition needing limited scheduled monitoring
Regular structured monitoring/coordination for one or more conditions
Frequent monitoring/coordination across interacting conditions
Very frequent/high-complexity monitoring approaching capability threshold

calibrationNote: Acute instability uses change-of-condition/capability pathway, not score inflation

Maintain stability of chronic conditions through regular structured monitoring and timely coordination of care.
Maintain clinical stability through frequent monitoring of interacting conditions, early recognition of deterioration and timely clinical coordination.
Maintain safety and clinical stability through very frequent structured monitoring, coordinated management and prompt escalation when needs approach service capability.
interventionDefaults: Perform routine wellness observation during normal care.
Encourage usual hydration, nutrition, activity and rest.
Record significant change from baseline.
Follow routine preventive/medical appointments as scheduled.
Complete limited scheduled monitoring for the identified stable condition.
Record ordered measurements and symptoms in the designated record.
Reinforce condition-specific self-management instructions within care scope.
Notify nurse/provider of readings/symptoms outside ordered parameters.
Carry out regular structured monitoring for one or more chronic conditions.
Trend ordered readings, symptoms, weight or intake where applicable.
Coordinate appointments/labs and ensure results/orders are communicated.
Escalate early changes before they become acute.
Perform frequent monitoring across interacting conditions using a documented schedule.
Compare current findings with resident-specific baseline and ordered parameters.
Coordinate medication, nutrition, hydration and appointment issues with nurse/provider.
Provide clear shift-to-shift handoff of active clinical concerns.
Provide very frequent structured clinical observation within service capability.
Maintain active interdisciplinary coordination and explicit escalation thresholds.
Document response to interventions and unresolved abnormalities.
Initiate emergency/transfer process when criteria are met.

name: Medication Support
anchors: Self-manages where permitted / no staff medication support
Routine low-complexity medication assistance/administration
Multiple scheduled meds or monitoring requiring regular staff oversight
High-risk/complex regimen with enhanced monitoring/reconciliation
Very high medication-management burden requiring intensive licensed oversight

Confirm resident has taken medication when supervision is part of plan.
Maintain consistent medication timing around resident routine.
Document refusals, omissions or unusual effects.
Provide regular medication supervision/assistance according to MAR/orders and scope.
Check the right resident/medication/time/route per medication policy.
Monitor for side effects, sedation, dizziness or behavior/cognition change.
Report refusals, omissions, PRN patterns and concerns to nurse/provider.
Use structured medication administration and reconciliation process for complex regimen.
Coordinate time-critical medications, monitoring and meals as ordered.
Track PRN use/response and high-risk side effects.
Ensure changes after hospital/clinic visits are reconciled before implementation.
Provide intensive medication support within licensed/service capability.
Maintain close observation for therapeutic response and serious adverse effects.
Use explicit escalation pathway for missed critical doses, reactions or clinical instability.
Coordinate promptly with prescriber/pharmacy/nurse for regimen issues.

name: Nutrition / Hydration

Setup/cueing or minor diet support
Regular meal assistance, supplementation or intake monitoring

Near-total feeding dependence or severe persistent nutrition/hydration burden within capability

Ensure water/beverages are accessible.

Provide meal setup, packaging assistance or cueing as needed.
Offer preferred fluids regularly and encourage adequate intake.
Follow prescribed diet texture/diet modifications if present.
Document persistent poor intake or new food difficulty.
Monitor meal/fluid intake and weight at care-plan frequency.
Provide regular meal assistance and prescribed nutritional supplements.
Offer nutrient-dense preferred foods and fluids within diet orders.
Escalate persistent low intake, weight loss, dehydration or glucose/meal mismatch.
Provide frequent individualized feeding/intake support and close monitoring.
Follow prescribed texture, positioning and swallowing precautions.
Track weight/intake/hydration trends and tolerance to supplements.
Coordinate clinical/dietitian/speech review for unresolved concerns.
Provide extensive feeding assistance while maintaining dignity and preferred pacing.
Follow all swallowing, texture, positioning and oral-care instructions.
Monitor tolerance, hydration, weight and signs of aspiration closely.

name: Communication
anchors: Communicates needs reliably
Minor hearing/speech/language barrier; simple adaptation
Regular communication support/cueing required
Major impairment requiring frequent interpretation/structured techniques
Unable to reliably express basic needs without intensive individualized support

Allow extra response time.
Use consistent communication aids/strategies across staff.
Present information in short phrases and confirm understanding.
Ensure sensory devices are maintained and available.
Document effective communication methods and resident preferences.
Use individualized communication plan during most interactions.
Anticipate needs and confirm through gestures, behavior and context.
Limit questions to one concept at a time and use visual/tactile cues as appropriate.
Coordinate speech/hearing/vision evaluation when indicated.
Use consistent individualized verbal and non-verbal communication at all care encounters.
Interpret behavior/non-verbal cues for pain, fear, hunger, toileting and comfort.
Offer simple choices using objects, pictures or gestures.
Share successful signals/cues across all caregivers.

name: Continence / Toileting

Occasional cueing/setup or rare accident assistance
Regular toileting assistance or continence care
Frequent hands-on toileting/diaper care with substantial workload
Near-total toileting/continence dependence with very high-frequency care

Provide regular toileting assistance or continence care on individualized schedule.

Change soiled products promptly and provide thorough gentle skin care.
Use safe transfer/repositioning plan for all toileting care.
Maintain dignity, privacy and comfort at each episode.

name: Skin Integrity

Risk factors requiring routine prevention/observation
Elevated risk requiring structured prevention/skin checks

name: Goals / Preferences / Decision Support
